architecture.mechanism: Real-time physiological intolerance monitoring to detect vascular occlusion onset immediately or within a defined delay threshold.
architecture.intervention: Integrate an inline pressure sensor with dual-threshold alarm logic that triggers immediate alert on rapid pressure rise (true occlusion) and a secondary 25-minute cumulative pressure integral alarm for delayed occlusion, while filtering transient spikes caused by patient movement via time-integration rather than instantaneous peak detection.
architecture.expected_effect: Downstream occlusions are detected either immediately or within 25 minutes before patient harm occurs, while transient pressure artifacts from patient movement do not trigger false alarms because they fail to sustain the required time-integrated pressure threshold.
architecture.falsification_test: Bench-test the infusion pump against a calibrated downstream occlusion simulator introducing both step-function total occlusions and transient pressure pulses mimicking patient movement; failure is declared if the system does not alarm within 25 minutes for true occlusion or issues a false alarm during transient movement simulation.
